newsitem.title: USA: Whitehall says Air Force reopens contract.
newsitem.headline: Whitehall says Air Force reopens contract.

text.p: Whitehall Corp said that the U.S. Air Force has decided to reopen a C-130 maintenance contract solicitation that had been won by its subsidiary.
The company said on Monday the Air Force decided to reopen the solicitation after an unsuccessful bidder issued a protest.
The contract, worth an estimated $100 million or more over five years, had been secured last month by its subsidiary, Aero Corp.

"We are surprised the Air Force is considering the action. However, in the interim, Aero will continue to make preparations to perform the contract," Whitehall chairman and chief executive George Baker said in a statement.
Whitehall did not name the unsuccessful bidder who issued the protest. It could not be reached immediately for comment.
Whitehall, through its subsidiary, rebuilds, modifies and maintains commercial and military aircraft.
